info.title: PostGrip Service API
info.description: Tenant-scoped service inventory, deployment, runtime control, and revision-fenced service administration.

post.summary: Preview and fence a multi-project release
post.description: Validates the complete dependency graph, exact revisions or artifacts, worker placement, current deployments, environment versions, verification policy, and overlap fences without dispatching work. Independent dependency-ready members form an explicit parallel group. An exact-commit member's `expectedCommitSha` must be the head of its `branch`, and is otherwise refused with `409` `SERVICE_STATE_CHANGED`. A member whose repository credential is held by its Worker (a private GitHub service bound to no GitHub installation, GitLab, or Bitbucket) has its head read by that Worker; a Worker that must be upgraded first fails the preview with `409` `WORKER_UPGRADE_REQUIRED`, and any other unreadable or moved head with `409` `SERVICE_STATE_CHANGED`. Such a member later fails with `REPOSITORY_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE` when its Worker holds no credential that can read the repository, `REPOSITORY_CREDENTIAL_DELIVERY_PENDING` while a supplied one is still being delivered, `SECRET_RESUBMISSION_REQUIRED` when it must be resubmitted, and `WORKER_UPGRADE_REQUIRED` when its Worker must be upgraded, with no build dispatched.

400.description: Invalid request. `VALIDATION`: the request is not a valid release group. `INVALID_BODY` also uses this status.

409.description: Conflict. `SERVICE_STATE_CHANGED`: a member's branch head does not match `expectedCommitSha` or could not be verified, or a member's placement, current deployment or source artifact does not match the request. `WORKER_UPGRADE_REQUIRED`: a member's Worker must be upgraded to read its branch head (`details.workerId`, `details.requiredCapability`). Other conflicts, such as `SERVICE_OPERATION_NOT_SUPPORTED`, `WORKER_UNAVAILABLE`, `REPOSITORY_UNAVAILABLE`, `SOURCE_ARTIFACT_NOT_READY` and `PUBLIC_VERIFICATION_UNAVAILABLE`, also use this status.

parameters.description: Only return release groups containing this project.

post.summary: Create a fenced multi-project release saga
post.description: Accepts an unexpired preview and creates one durable release identity. Dependency-ready members dispatch in parallel. A required failure cancels safe work and restores already-cut-over reversible members; non-reversible cutovers report intervention-required.

get.summary: Get aggregate and per-member release state

post.summary: Cancel and compensate a release group
post.description: Cancels undispatched and still-queued members, waits for unsafe-to-cancel members, and restores every reversible member that cut over.

post.summary: Retry a safely recovered release group
post.description: Retries the same pinned revisions only after compensation or cancellation reached a safe terminal state. Intervention-required groups require a new preview.

get.summary: Resolve a deploy request to an immutable commit
get.description: Resolves a deploy request to an environment and the immutable head commit of its branch, which deployService then confirms as `expectedCommitSha`. For a private GitHub service bound to no GitHub installation, and for GitLab and Bitbucket services, the service's repository credential is held only by its Workers, so the environment's Worker reads the branch head with it and returns only the commit. The preview fails with `409` `WORKER_UPGRADE_REQUIRED` (with `details.workerId` and `details.requiredCapability: "repository_head_read_v1"`) when that Worker must be upgraded first, `409` `NO_ELIGIBLE_WORKER` when no Worker can read it, and `409` `REPOSITORY_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE` when the Worker's credential cannot read the repository. The message then names what the target Worker needs: while a supplied credential is being delivered, wait for it; when it awaits resubmission, resubmit it; with none, or one the repository refuses, supply one (or bind the service to a GitHub account). To deploy a commit without reading the branch head, send it to deployService with `namedCommit: true`.

409.description: Conflict. `REPOSITORY_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE`: PostGrip cannot obtain the credential it needs to read the branch head, or the Worker that holds the service's credential cannot read the repository with it (the message names what the target Worker needs). `WORKER_UPGRADE_REQUIRED`: the Worker that must read the head does not advertise `repository_head_read_v1` (`details.workerId`, `details.requiredCapability`). `NO_ELIGIBLE_WORKER`: no Worker can read the head. Other conflicts, such as `SERVICE_OPERATION_NOT_SUPPORTED` and `SERVICE_ENVIRONMENT_REQUIRED`, also use this status.

post.summary: Queue a deployment for a confirmed commit
post.description: Queues a deployment of a confirmed commit to one environment. `expectedCommitSha` must equal the branch head previewServiceDeploy resolved (otherwise `409` `SERVICE_STATE_CHANGED`); for a service whose repository credential is held by its Workers, the environment's Worker reads that head. With `namedCommit: true`, `expectedCommitSha` is deployed as given without reading the branch head: it must then be a full 40-character hexadecimal commit SHA (otherwise `400` `VALIDATION`) and is normalized to lowercase, and `branch`, or else the default branch, is recorded unverified. A private GitHub service deploys with the repository credential supplied to the target Worker when that Worker holds one. A deployment never mints an installation token over a supplied credential, including for a service adopted from a GitHub installation; only adoption or rebinding the service moves it back to its installation. The request fails with `409` and queues nothing when the supplied credential cannot be used: `SECRET_RESUBMISSION_REQUIRED` when it awaits resubmission or a re-send of it failed, and `REPOSITORY_CREDENTIAL_DELIVERY_PENDING` with `Retry-After` while it is still being delivered, whether the service is bound to no GitHub installation, adopted from one, or bound to one from the console. For a service whose repository credential is held by its Workers, `REPOSITORY_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE` means the target Worker holds no credential, or one the repository refuses. A Worker that must read the head and does not advertise `repository_head_read_v1` fails the request with `409` `WORKER_UPGRADE_REQUIRED`, and no Worker able to read it with `409` `NO_ELIGIBLE_WORKER`. None of these refusals consumes the Idempotency-Key: resubmit or supply the credential with putServiceRepositoryCredential (`source-access`), bind the service, wait for the delivery, or upgrade or assign the Worker, then retry the request, with the same key if you like.

400.description: Invalid request. `VALIDATION`: `namedCommit` is set and `expectedCommitSha` is not a full 40-character hexadecimal commit SHA. Other invalid requests, such as `INVALID_BODY` and `INVALID_BRANCH`, also use this status.

409.description: Conflict. These refusals queue nothing and are not stored against the Idempotency-Key, so a retry with the same key runs the request again: `SECRET_RESUBMISSION_REQUIRED`, the target Worker's supplied repository credential awaits resubmission or a re-send of it failed (resubmit it with putServiceRepositoryCredential, `source-access`); `REPOSITORY_CREDENTIAL_DELIVERY_PENDING`, the Worker's supplied credential is still being delivered (retry after `Retry-After` seconds); `REPOSITORY_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE`, the Worker that holds the service's credential holds none, or holds one the repository refuses (supply one with putServiceRepositoryCredential, `source-access`, or bind the service); `WORKER_UPGRADE_REQUIRED`, that Worker must be upgraded to read the branch head (`details.workerId`, `details.requiredCapability`); `NO_ELIGIBLE_WORKER`, no Worker can read the branch head; `WRITE_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`, a LadybugDB service's starter Compose file write reached the target Worker and its answer was lost, so the file may or may not have been written, and nothing was deployed (a retry rereads the file before it deploys). `REPOSITORY_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE` is also returned, and stored against the key like other conflicts, when PostGrip cannot obtain the credential it needs to read the branch head. Other conflicts on this route, such as `SERVICE_STATE_CHANGED`, `SERVICE_ENVIRONMENT_REQUIRED`, `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT` and `IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS`, also use this status.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. Sent with `REPOSITORY_CREDENTIAL_DELIVERY_PENDING` and `IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS`.

409.description: Conflict. `WORKER_REVOKED`: `workerId` names a revoked Worker (`details.workerId`). Revoked is terminal: enroll a new Worker or replace the revoked one. The refusal is permanent, so a retry with the same Idempotency-Key replays it. A removed or replaced Worker, including one that is also revoked, answers `404` `NOT_FOUND`. `WORKER_UPGRADE_REQUIRED`: the Worker does not advertise a capability the operation needs (`details.workerId`, `details.requiredCapability`); upgrade the Worker and retry. This refusal is not stored against the Idempotency-Key, so a retry with the same key runs again. Other conflicts on this route also use this status.

Conflict. `TARGET_CREATION_PENDING`: a keyed creation of the target (the console's `POST /api/targets` with an `Idempotency-Key`) is still pending, so the target can't be changed yet. Nothing is changed or queued, and the refusal is not stored against the Idempotency-Key: retry with the same key once the creation settles. `WORKER_UPGRADE_REQUIRED`: the target's Worker does not advertise a capability the change needs (`details.workerId`, `details.requiredCapability`); this refusal is not stored against the key either. Other conflicts, such as `SERVICE_STATE_CHANGED`, also use this status.

Conflict. `TARGET_CREATION_PENDING`: a keyed creation of the target (the console's `POST /api/targets` with an `Idempotency-Key`) is still pending, so its connection can't be set yet. Other conflicts, such as `SERVICE_STATE_CHANGED`, also use this status.

Conflict. `WORKER_REVOKED`: `defaultWorkerId` names a Worker that was revoked after the request's pre-check (`details.workerId`); revoked is terminal. `NO_ELIGIBLE_WORKER`: `defaultWorkerId` names a Worker that is not trusted, recently online and capable, including one already revoked, removed or replaced. `WORKER_UPGRADE_REQUIRED`: the Worker runs a version below the one the control plane expects; upgrade the Worker and retry. `NO_ELIGIBLE_WORKER` and `WORKER_UPGRADE_REQUIRED` are not stored against the Idempotency-Key, so a retry with the same key runs again. Conflict. `WORKER_REVOKED` (`details.workerId`): with `assignedWorkerId`, that Worker is revoked; revoked is terminal (enroll a new Worker or replace the revoked one), so the refusal is stored against the Idempotency-Key and replays. Without `assignedWorkerId`, the Worker selection chose (the project default or automatic placement) was revoked before the placement locked it; that refusal is not stored against the key, so a retry with the same key selects again. `NO_ELIGIBLE_WORKER` (`details.requiredCapabilities`, `details.defaultWorkerId`): no Worker is eligible, or the Worker placement chose was removed, replaced or became ineligible after the request's pre-check, including a removed or replaced project default. Placement does not reselect, but the refusal is not stored against the key, so a retry with the same key selects again. `WORKER_UPGRADE_REQUIRED`: with `assignedWorkerId`, that Worker does not advertise a capability the operation needs (`details.workerId`, `details.requiredCapability`); without it, the project default or automatic candidate runs a version below the one the control plane expects (`details.requiredCapabilities`). Upgrade the Worker and retry; the refusal is not stored against the key, so a retry with the same key runs again. `404` `NOT_FOUND` applies only to an explicit `assignedWorkerId` already removed or replaced when the request arrived, including one that is also revoked. get.description: Returns the latest bounded public DNS, TLS, route, and HTTP observation for the configured domain. This evidence is separate from runtime readiness.

post.description: Performs a bounded HTTPS request to the saved tenant domain only, persists deployment- and configuration-version-bound observations, and advances domain verification and route state when the target is still current.

400.description: Invalid request. `VALIDATION`: the update names no field, its `name` is not a valid variable name, or it sets `isSecret` to `false` on a secret variable that has a value. A secret's value is never shown, so it cannot become a non-secret value by this update: set the variable's new value in the same change with `applyServiceVariables`, giving the variable's existing `variableId` with `isSecret: false` and the new `value` (without `variableId` the apply creates a new variable, and the existing name makes it fail with `409 SERVICE_STATE_CHANGED`), or clear its value first (`clearServiceVariableValue`) and then update it. `INVALID_BODY` also uses this status.

get.description: Lists repositories visible through one connected GitHub account (installation) of the tenant. Pass installationRef when the tenant has several active accounts; a tenant with one account needs no selector, and a cursor alone continues the installation it was issued for. Refusals: 400 GITHUB_INSTALLATION_SELECTOR_REQUIRED (several accounts and no installationRef or cursor), 400 INVALID_INSTALLATION_REF, 400 INVALID_CURSOR (malformed, another tenant, or issued for an installation other than installationRef), 410 CURSOR_EXPIRED (24 hours), and 409 GITHUB_INSTALLATION_REQUIRED (the selected installation is not an active account of the tenant, including a disconnected or revoked one). There is no cursor across accounts.

200.description: Bounded repositories visible through the tenant GitHub App installation

post.description: Records an expiring adoption preview against exactly one GitHub account of the tenant. The account is installationRef when given, else the one active account whose login owns an owner/name repository, else the tenant's only account; a repositoryId selection carries no owner, so a tenant with several accounts names the account with installationRef. Refusals: 400 GITHUB_INSTALLATION_SELECTOR_REQUIRED (several accounts and the request resolves none), 400 INVALID_INSTALLATION_REF, and 409 GITHUB_INSTALLATION_REQUIRED (installationRef is not an active account of the tenant).

Adopts the repository of an accepted preview through the installation that preview was created under, which must still be an active account of the tenant (409 GITHUB_INSTALLATION_REQUIRED otherwise; another account is never substituted). A repository already adopted by another service of the tenant is 409 GITHUB_ADOPTION_CONFLICT, including a preview blocked as adopted-other-project; organizations sharing one installation each adopt independently.

Refreshes the repository credential on the service's assigned Workers. `webhook-signing` generates a new webhook signing secret. `source-access` issues a new token from the GitHub installation the project is bound to and never replaces a supplied credential: a Worker whose credential is supplied is skipped and sent nothing, and its target in the staged configuration operation is `succeeded` with `errorCode` `CREDENTIAL_SOURCE_SUPPLIED`. When no Worker can be refreshed from an installation and at least one was skipped because its credential is supplied, which is every Worker when the project is not bound to an installation, the request fails with `409` `CREDENTIAL_SOURCE_SUPPLIED` and stages no operation. A supplied credential is refreshed by resubmitting it with putServiceRepositoryCredential.

409.description: Conflict. `CREDENTIAL_SOURCE_SUPPLIED`: `credentialKind` is `source-access`, no Worker can be refreshed from a GitHub installation, and at least one Worker's credential is supplied (every Worker's, when the project is not bound to an installation). No configuration operation is staged; resubmit the credential with putServiceRepositoryCredential to refresh it. Other conflicts on this route, such as `SERVICE_STATE_CHANGED` and `SERVICE_OPERATION_NOT_SUPPORTED`, also use this status.

Accepts an observed result only when it reports every derived record exactly once and contains no extra mutation. Successful reports enter bounded propagation and public verification.

get.description: Lists branches through one connected GitHub account of the tenant without exposing installation credentials. The account is installationRef when given, else the one active account whose login is owner, else the tenant's only account. Refusals: 400 GITHUB_INSTALLATION_SELECTOR_REQUIRED, 400 INVALID_INSTALLATION_REF, 400 GITHUB_NOT_CONNECTED (no account), 409 GITHUB_INSTALLATION_REQUIRED (installationRef is not an active account), and 422 GITHUB_REPOSITORY_NOT_VISIBLE.

GitHubInstallationRef.name: installationRef
GitHubInstallationRef.description: The connected GitHub account (installation) to act through. Required only when the tenant has several active accounts and the request is not otherwise resolved to one.

expectedCommitSha.description: The commit to deploy, with `branch`. It must be the head of `branch`; for a service whose repository credential is held only by its Workers, the member's Worker reads that head.

reversible.description: Set false for stateful members that must never be silently rolled back. A cutover followed by group failure then reports intervention_required.

errorDetail.description: Safe bounded release detail; Worker errors and secrets are not exposed.

cutoverState.description: The deployment's role in the production cutover lifecycle. A candidate is building but cannot receive traffic, cutover is ready and switching, rollback_candidate is an explicit rollback that is queued or building and cannot receive traffic, rollback_cutover is an explicit rollback whose target is ready and switching, live is the routed deployment, retained is the one last known-good rollback target, historical is a completed deployment whose runtime is not retained, and terminal is an incomplete deployment that is neither routed nor retained.

namedCommit.description: Deploy expectedCommitSha as given, without reading the branch head. It must then be a full 40-character hexadecimal commit SHA (otherwise 400 VALIDATION); the branch is recorded unverified.

defaultWorkerId.description: Eligible project-level Worker override used for future environment placement when assignedWorkerId is omitted.
Sets the eligible project-level Worker override. This placement change additionally requires services:admin.

clearDefaultWorker.description: Clears the project Worker default so future environments return to automatic placement. Setting this to true additionally requires services:admin.

assignedWorkerId.description: Explicit placement override. When omitted, the project default or deterministic automatic placement is used.

volumes.description: Worker-scoped ephemeral bind mounts. The server derives tenant/project/environment-scoped storage paths from containerPath; Worker-local paths are never accepted or returned.
Replaces the environment's Worker-scoped ephemeral bind mounts. This field requires services:admin.

isSecret.description: Whether the variable is secret. Setting it to `false` on a secret variable that has a value is refused (`400 VALIDATION`): the value was stored as a secret and is never shown, so making it non-secret requires a new value. Use `applyServiceVariables` with the variable's existing `variableId`, `isSecret: false` and the new `value` (without `variableId` the apply creates a new variable and fails with `409 SERVICE_STATE_CHANGED`), or clear the value first with `clearServiceVariableValue`. A secret without a value can be made non-secret here.

installationRef.description: The connected GitHub account to adopt through. Required only when the tenant has several active accounts and the owner of an owner/name repository does not select one.

ServiceAppDeletionResponse.description: Deletion result for a grouping whose attached projects and target services are retained and detached.

ServiceAutomaticDeploymentWiring.description: Last reconciled state of push-triggered automatic deployment wiring. Credential presence alone does not imply that the provider can reach or is configured to call PostGrip.

reason.description: Stable audit reason for the resolved placement decision.

canonicalDnsDomainIds.description: Canonical DNS domains whose active or recoverable target blocks this removal until it is reconciled.

errorCode.description: Machine-readable code for the target's outcome, normally set when the target failed or is blocked. A `succeeded` target of a `repository-credential-refresh` operation with `CREDENTIAL_SOURCE_SUPPLIED` is a Worker skipped because its `source-access` credential is supplied: it was sent nothing and kept that credential. A `blocked` target of a repository credential put, clear or refresh, a GitHub repository adoption, or a configuration apply with `CREDENTIAL_SUPERSEDED` is a Worker whose credential a newer decision for the same service already owns: this obsolete intent was not delivered, the Worker keeps the newer decision's credential, and nothing needs to be retried. A `succeeded` target of a deletion (an operation whose kind ends in `-delete`) with `WORKER_CLEANUP_SKIPPED` is a Worker that is gone, removed, replaced or revoked: the deletion completed in the control plane and nothing was sent to that Worker. `WORKER_UNAVAILABLE` on a `blocked` target has two meanings. On a repository-credential target it is a live Worker whose delivery attempts were exhausted, recoverable once the Worker is reachable: for a clear or removal target, retry the cleanup; for an issue target (a put, refresh or adoption), make a new credential decision by repeating the put or refresh. On any other target it is a Worker that is gone, removed, replaced or revoked, which no retry can reach.

lastErrorCode.description: Machine-readable code of the operation's last failure or block, as on its targets. `CREDENTIAL_SUPERSEDED` means a newer repository credential decision for the same service and Worker (a later put, clear, refresh, adoption or configuration apply) already owns that Worker's credential: this obsolete intent was not delivered, the Worker keeps the newer decision's credential, and nothing needs to be retried.

outputDir.description: Static build output directory relative to the repository's configured projectPath. Empty values use the imperative default; non-empty values cannot be absolute, resolve to the project workspace root, or traverse parent directories. Static deployments require build in WORKER_CAPABILITIES and WORKER_UNSAFE_HOST_BUILDS_ENABLED=true on the assigned Worker.

deploymentMode.description: Static mode is supported only for web projects whose framework does not require Docker.

allowRemoval.description: Explicitly authorizes removal of stack-owned projects and environments that are absent from the manifest. Requires prune=true.

removalDataDisposition.description: Required when an explicitly removed project or environment has managed volumes. The selected disposition is fenced into the immutable plan.

reason.description: Why the action has its kind. For a repository `.github` action (the GitHub App reconcile) that GitHub planning blocked: `GITHUB_INSTALLATION_SELECTOR_REQUIRED` (several connected GitHub accounts, and neither the project's binding nor the repository owner selects one), `GITHUB_INSTALLATION_REQUIRED` (the selected account is not an active account of the tenant), `GITHUB_PERMISSION_REQUIRED` or `GITHUB_REPOSITORY_NOT_AUTHORIZED`.

lastErrorCode.description: When the operation is `blocked`, the code of its first blocked action (in action order), as on that action's `lastErrorCode`, or `CONFIGURATION_ACTION_BLOCKED` when the action recorded none; `CONFIGURATION_ACTION_FAILED` when it failed. `CREDENTIAL_SUPERSEDED` means a newer repository credential decision for the same service and Worker already owns that Worker's credential: the obsolete intent was not delivered, the Worker keeps the newer decision's credential, and nothing needs to be retried.

Machine-readable code for the action's last failure or block, including the code of the Service operation it staged. `CREDENTIAL_SUPERSEDED` means a newer repository credential decision for the same service and Worker (a later put, clear, refresh, adoption or configuration apply) already owns that Worker's credential: this obsolete intent was not delivered, the Worker keeps the newer decision's credential, and nothing needs to be retried.

ServiceEphemeralVolumeMount.description: Public projection of a Worker-scoped ephemeral mount. Worker-local storage paths are intentionally omitted.

value.description: Present only for variables explicitly marked non-secret.
